terms.grammar: adjective; incertum est with a question: it is unclear whether …
evidence: Cic. Sen. 74: et incertum an hoc ipsō diē
Plin. Ep. 4.11.5 (Lewis & Short): incertum, utrum quia vērum erat

terms.gloss: doubtful, uncertain; dubium est, it is uncertain
terms.grammar: adjective; dubium est with a question

terms.gloss: it is not clear, not proven
terms.grammar: impersonal of liqueō, alone or with a question
evidence: Cic. Div. 1.6: dē quō Panaetiō nōn liquet
terms.comment: First the verdict of a juror who could not decide: nōn liquēre dīxērunt (Cic. Clu. 76, Lewis & Short). Liquet, it is clear (Plaut., Cic.).

evidence: Cic. Marcell. 5: incertus exitus et anceps fortūna bellī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “two-headed”; of an outcome that could go either way. In the sense “dangerous” Lewis & Short calls it post-Augustan and never Ciceronian.

phrases.latin: moriendum enim certē est, et incertum an hoc ipsō diē
phrases.english: for die we certainly must, and it is uncertain whether it may not be this very day

phrases.latin: quod crepusculum diēs etiam nunc sit an jam nox multīs dubium
phrases.english: because at dusk many are unsure whether it is still day or already night

phrases.latin: praesertim cum id, dē quō Panaetiō nōn liquet, reliquīs ejusdem disciplīnae sōlis lūce videātur clārius
phrases.english: especially since what is unclear to Panaetius seems clearer than daylight to the rest of his school
